title: Fix AI Chat Reasoning Display with Vercel AI SDK Data Stream Protocol
body:
Fixes the reasoning/thinking display in the Studio AI chat by correcting both the backend stream encoding and frontend parsing to align with the Vercel AI SDK v6 Data Stream Protocol.

## Problem

The AI chat panel was only showing "thinking" without displaying actual reasoning content or step progress indicators. This was due to a protocol mismatch between how the backend encoded reasoning events and how the frontend parsed them.

## Root Cause

1. **Backend**: Was encoding reasoning events in standard SSE format (`data: {"type":"reasoning-delta",...}`) instead of Vercel AI SDK Data Stream Protocol format
2. **Frontend**: Was attempting to access reasoning through the `data` property instead of the `message.parts` array where it actually appears

## Changes Made

### Backend (packages/services/service-ai/)

- **vercel-stream-encoder.ts**: 
  - Added `dataStreamLine()` helper function for Data Stream Protocol formatting
  - Fixed reasoning event encoding to use `g:` prefix:
    - `reasoning-start` → `g:{"text":""}\n`
    - `reasoning-delta` → `g:{"text":"..."}\n`
    - `reasoning-end` → empty string
  - Aligns with Vercel AI SDK protocol specification

- **__tests__/vercel-stream-encoder.test.ts**:
  - Updated tests to expect `g:` prefix format for reasoning events
  - All 17 tests passing

### Frontend (apps/studio/)

- **AiChatPanel.tsx**:
  - Changed to extract reasoning from `message.parts` array instead of `data` property
  - Process `reasoning-delta`/`reasoning` parts for thinking display
  - Process `step-start`/`step-finish` parts for progress tracking
  - Removed unused stream event type interfaces (fixed TypeScript warnings)

## Technical Details

The Vercel AI SDK v6 Data Stream Protocol uses prefix identifiers:
- `0:` - Text content
- `2:` - Custom data annotations
- `g:` - Reasoning/thinking content (DeepSeek R1, OpenAI o1-style models)

The backend now correctly encodes reasoning using the Data Stream Protocol format, and the frontend properly parses it from the `message.parts` array.

## Testing

- ✅ All stream encoder tests pass (17/17)
- ✅ TypeScript compilation clean for modified files
- ✅ Reasoning display should now work correctly with models that support reasoning streams (DeepSeek R1, OpenAI o1-style models)
